system_prompt:
You are a senior systems architect compiling a dense Architectural Fact Sheet from project documents.
Compile:
1. Core Business Goals (exactly 5 specific items)
2. Primary User Personas & Entry Points
3. Identified Pain Points & Constraints (exactly 5 specific items)
4. Key Technology Stack preferences (Frontend, Backend, DB)
5. Critical Security & Performance NFRs

Return ONLY valid JSON with these fields. No explanations.

core_business_goals: Automate similarity scoring between Power BI report metadata fields to reduce manual mapping effort
Produce structured Excel exports containing field-level similarity scores for downstream consumption
Leverage hybrid ML pipeline (TF-IDF + Jaccard + Levenshtein) to deliver accurate attribute matching without pre-trained model dependencies
Augment ML scoring with LLM-based semantic equivalence detection using Azure AI Foundry Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
Provide an accessible, browser-based SPA interface for analysts to upload, review, and filter report mapping results

personas.name: BI Analyst / Report Developer
personas.description: Uploads exported Power BI metadata files and reviews field similarity results to validate or reconcile report schemas
personas.entry_point: Client-side SPA (HTML5/Bootstrap 5.3) accessed via browser; file upload triggers Flask API pipeline

personas.name: Data Governance / Migration Engineer
personas.description: Consumes structured Excel output with similarity scores to drive field mapping decisions during Power BI migrations or consolidations
personas.entry_point: Downloaded Excel export generated by Flask backend after pipeline execution

identified_pain_points_and_constraints: Critical security vulnerability: Azure OpenAI API key is hardcoded in server.py and must be externalized to environment variables or a secrets manager before any production deployment
LLM throughput is constrained by batching (25 pairs per batch) and limited parallelism (ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers=2), creating potential latency bottlenecks on large input files
No pre-trained or cached models exist; TF-IDF vectorizer is rebuilt at request time from the full input corpus, increasing per-request compute cost
Tool depends entirely on manually exported Excel/CSV metadata files with no live Power BI service API integration, requiring users to maintain an offline export workflow
UI is constrained to a 1200px max-width layout with no stated responsive/mobile breakpoint strategy, limiting usability on non-desktop viewports

key_technology_stack_preferences.frontend: Client-side SPA using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Bootstrap 5.3; no server-side rendering; CSS custom properties for theming; max-width 1200px layout with searchable/sortable/filterable report cards and tabbed views
key_technology_stack_preferences.backend: Python Flask API (server.py) handling file ingestion, ML pipeline orchestration, LLM call management, and Excel export generation; ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel LLM batching; exponential backoff retry logic (3 attempts)
key_technology_stack_preferences.database: No persistent database; stateless request-time processing using in-memory TF-IDF vectorizer built from input corpus; input via Excel/CSV files; output via structured Excel export

security: Azure OpenAI API key must be removed from source code and stored in environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager prior to production release
No direct Power BI service API dependency eliminates OAuth/service principal attack surface; all data handled as static file uploads
performance: LLM scoring applied conditionally only when confidence threshold is met; hybrid ML score used as fallback if LLM is unavailable, ensuring pipeline resilience
LLM calls batched in groups of 25 pairs with max_workers=2 parallelism and 3-attempt exponential backoff to balance throughput against API rate limits
TF-IDF vectorizer uses character n-grams (2–4) built at request time; performance scales with corpus size and must be monitored for large metadata files
Hybrid scoring weights (TF-IDF 45%, Jaccard trigram 30%, Levenshtein 25%) must remain tunable to adapt accuracy vs. speed trade-offs without redeployment
